summary:
Iteration 9 (favorites + cancellation fee + driver stats + public ride sharing): Backend PASS 11/11 pytest (/app/backend/tests/test_passenger_extras.py, -n 0, 8.9 s wall). Frontend web (390×844) — all critical NEW flows verified against public preview.

BACKEND — (1) Favorites: POST /api/favorites replaces same-label entry (2 successive POST 'Maison' → GET returns exactly one Maison with the latest address, previous id gone). DELETE unknown-id → 404, DELETE own id → 200 and disappears from GET. (2) Cancellation: passenger creates ride (Paris → Arc de Triomphe cash), immediate cancel → 200 with cancellation_fee 0. Second ride accepted by chauffeur@test.com then passenger cancel → 200 with cancellation_fee=3.0 exact. Third ride accepted+started then passenger cancel → 409 'Impossible d'annuler une course en cours'. GET /api/driver/earnings returns cancellation_fees ≥ 3.0. (3) Decline+stats: POST /api/rides/{id}/decline → 200 and that ride no longer appears in GET /api/rides/available for that driver (verified id-not-in-list). Decline unknown ride → 404. GET /api/driver/stats returns online_hours_week/total, acceptance_rate (int or null), accepted, declined ≥ 1 after the decline test, best_slots (list), earnings_by_day (list length 7 with day/amount). Toggle offline (closes session, persists to driver_sessions with end=now) → online_hours_total non-decreasing. (4) Public tracking: GET /api/public/track/{share_token} WITHOUT Authorization → 200 with status/pickup.address/dropoff.address, and passenger_id/passenger_phone are NOT in the payload (whitelist projection in passenger_extras.public_track). Bad token → 404.

FRONTEND (390×844, Chromium) — (a) FAVORITES: login as passager@test.com → passenger-home → tap destination-search → type 'Gare' → 7 places show fav-save-{id}. Tap the first fav-save → save-favorite modal opens → fav-label-Travail → fav-submit → clear query → 'Travail' row appears at the top of the list with a briefcase icon + fav-delete-{id} trash button (screenshot /tmp/favs.png). fav-delete → row disappears (count 1 → 0). (b) RIDE + SHARE: destination-search → place-1 (Tour Eiffel) → confirm-ride-button. ride-detail loads with 'Recherche d'un chauffeur…', share-trip button visible, cancel hint 'Annulation gratuite tant qu'aucun chauffeur n'a accepté'. Fetched share_token via /api/rides/{id} (bearer) then opened /track/{share_token} in a new tab WITHOUT logging in → public-track testID visible, 'Recherche d'un chauffeur…' + 'Châtelet, 75001 Paris' + 'Champ de Mars…' rendered (screenshot /tmp/public_track.png). (c) DRIVER ACCEPTS → PASSENGER FEE HINT: called /api/rides/{id}/accept as chauffeur@test.com; passenger ride-detail polling refreshed → driver card 'Chauffeur en route · Peugeot 508 · AB-123-CD' + cancel hint '⚠️ Frais d'annulation : 3,00 € (chauffeur déjà en route)' (screenshot /tmp/after_accept.png). Passenger tap cancel-ride → window.confirm accepted → cancel POST fires (verified backend); router.replace to rides list races the URL assertion (still at /ride/{id} at read time, not a bug — see action_items). (d) DRIVER STATS: login chauffeur@test.com → Gains tab → driver-stats section visible: 'En ligne (7 j)' + '0 h au total' cell, 'Acceptation 86 %', '12 acceptées · 2 refusées', 'Meilleurs créneaux de la semaine' with 3 rows, and the cancellation-fee line '+ 6.00 € de frais d'annulation perçus' (screenshot /tmp/stats.png). (e) DRIVER DECLINE BUTTON: verified in code at /app/frontend/app/(driver)/index.tsx as testID `decline-{ride.id}` (Pressable calling POST /rides/{id}/decline then setRides filter). Live UI verification skipped this run — driver had an active accepted ride from the earlier flow that hides the offers list; backend equivalent already covered by TestDeclineAndStats.test_decline_hides_ride (green).

No functional regressions detected. React-19 ref deprecation warning still emitted (carry-over from iterations 6+8).
action_items: LOW (test-authoring only): after passenger cancels an accepted ride, the ride-detail screen does router.replace('/(passenger)/rides') but the polling interval may fire load() one more time before the replace commits, so the URL stays on /ride/{id} for ~1 s. Not a bug — the ride is cancelled server-side (verified) and 'Annulée' appears on the rides list after ~2 s. Main agent can add a stopPolling flag inside doCancel before the router.replace if you want the transition to feel instant.

LOW (carry-over, React 19 deprecation warning): 'Accessing element.ref was removed in React 19. ref is now a regular prop' still surfaces on the login screen and passenger home. Same as iterations 6/8 — no user-visible impact.

LOW (test coverage gap): driver-home decline-{id} button was not exercised live this run because the chauffeur@test.com driver still had an accepted ride from the fee-cancellation flow at that point, hiding the offers card. To reproduce in the UI: log in as driver on a clean session (no active ride) with the driver online, create a passenger ride, then tap decline-{id} — the card disappears immediately (state filter in /app/frontend/app/(driver)/index.tsx). Backend behaviour is covered by pytest TestDeclineAndStats.
critical_code_review_comments: passenger_extras.add_favorite deletes then inserts under the same (user_id,label) — correct upsert-like semantics, but two very fast concurrent POSTs on 'Maison' could still both delete and both insert (race). Not exploitable via the current UI (button is disabled during the await), and both docs would share user_id+label — a unique index on (user_id,label) would harden it. Add: db.favorites.create_index([('user_id',1),('label',1)], unique=True).

passenger_extras.public_track uses an explicit whitelist projection (passenger_name kept, passenger_id/phone dropped). Test test_public_track_no_auth_exposes_only_safe_fields asserts absence of both sensitive keys — green. share_token is 12-byte URL-safe (~72 bits, secrets.token_urlsafe(12)) which is sufficient for un-guessability; consider rotating on ride status transitions if the same passenger repeatedly rides.

rides.cancel_ride correctly returns 409 when passenger tries to cancel an in_progress ride but the driver can still cancel (line 234 checks user==passenger). Cancellation fee is only applied when status=='accepted' AND user==passenger AND ride.driver_id present — matches spec. Fee currently constant (CANCEL_FEE=3.0). Consider promoting to per-city config later.

driver.driver_status closes the online session synchronously and inserts into db.driver_sessions on offline transition — good. If the app crashes while online, `online_since` remains set and driver_stats._aware() will keep accruing the open interval indefinitely; add a background job that closes sessions older than 24 h, or clamp _aware() to min(now, start+8h).

passenger_extras.driver_stats iterates rides twice (best_slots + by_day) in a single find loop and is O(rides). Acceptable up to a few thousand completed rides per driver. If it grows, precompute a daily aggregate.
Frontend: passenger-home.saveFavorite catches errors and Alert-flashes them — good UX. removeFavorite silently swallows failures ('} catch {}'). Consider a small toast for the delete-unknown case.

success_rate.backend: 100% (11/11 pytest, 30+ assertions covering favorites CRUD/upsert, cancellation-fee matrix, decline visibility, stats shape, online-session accumulation, public tracking without auth + field whitelist)
success_rate.frontend: ~92% (favorites save+delete flow, ride create with share-trip + cancel hint copy, public /track/{token} no-auth render, 3 € fee hint after driver acceptance, driver stats page with online/acceptance/best-slots/cancellation-fees line — all visually verified. Decline button live-tap skipped due to driver state carry-over, code path reviewed and backend covered.)

seed_data_creation: Created and cleaned up two throwaway passenger favorites 'Maison' (upsert test — final DELETE) and one 'Travail' (UI flow — deleted via UI). Created 3 passenger rides during the run: (1) requested→cancelled (fee 0), (2) accepted→cancelled by passenger (fee 3, kept on chauffeur@test.com earnings), (3) accepted→started→cancel 409 then driver /complete. The UI test also created 2 more rides (fee-hint flow + decline flow) — both cancelled at teardown. chauffeur@test.com is left online with rating/vehicle untouched; +6.00 € cancellation_fees now visible on their earnings (accumulates run-over-run — not a leak, it's the intended feature).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `pytest backend/tests/test_passenger_extras.py -n 0 -v` — module fixture drv_tok cleans up leftover active rides and pings /driver/status is_online=true, so it is idempotent even after crashed previous runs. If you extend the pytest to cover driver stats deltas, remember that online_hours_total only ticks up after a full online→offline cycle (the open session's minutes are counted live inside driver_stats but not persisted). For frontend, to hit the driver-decline flow reliably: (1) POST /api/rides/{d}/cancel on every ride in /rides/active-list for chauffeur@test.com before the driver logs in, (2) then create a fresh passenger ride, (3) navigate driver to /accueil — the offer card appears in ≈2 s and decline-{id} is a Pressable inside it. window.confirm is used for cancellation in ride-detail — always register `page.on('dialog', lambda d: d.accept())` before clicking cancel-ride.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs surfaced. Two test-authoring nits: (i) after tapping cancel-ride the URL race with router.replace can make an immediate `page.url` read still show /ride/{id}; solution: wait_for_url('**/rides**') for up to 3 s. (ii) On a shared preview environment the chauffeur@test.com account can carry an accepted ride between iterations; always run the cleanup snippet from the module fixture before UI-testing driver-home offers.
